_coverage_rationale: REF-DEAL-7: Company with quarterly actuals + annual forecast rows + mixed currency/unit labeling in the same XLSX workbook. Tests three failure modes that none of the existing 4 deals exercise: (1) quarterly period labels ('Q1 2024', 'Q3 2024 Actual') vs annual labels ('FY2025E') in identical columns — verifies the system builds correct period_type and picks LTM actuals, not Q1 data, for current state; (2) mixed unit labeling — one sheet in whole dollars, another sheet in $000s — verifies the scale-detection guard prevents a $3,200 (thousands) number from being stored as $3,200 instead of $3,200,000; (3) multi-currency — XLSX has USD revenue and GBP cost-of-goods at a stated exchange rate — verifies the system normalizes to USD before computing burn or gross margin.
_failure_modes_targeted: Quarter-as-current: Q1 actual selected as current_state instead of most-recent LTM or trailing-twelve-months total
Quarter-inflation: four quarterly rows summed incorrectly into an annualized figure 4x actual revenue
Scale-mixing: one XLSX sheet using $000s denomination, another using whole dollars — both on the same workbook
Multi-currency: USD revenue sheet + GBP COGS sheet; burn_rate computed in wrong currency
Forward annual mixed with quarterly actuals: 'FY2025E' budget row adjacent to Q4 2024 actual — compiler prefers the budget year over the actual trailing data
Unit label guard miss: a row labeled 'Q3 2024 Revenue ($000s)' being extracted as revenue=Q3value instead of Q3value*1000

financials._currency_note: __FILL IN — state which sheets are USD vs GBP and the stated exchange rate if provided__

revenue.value: __FILL IN — FY2024 Actual total revenue (full year, NOT one quarter, in USD whole dollars)__
revenue.evidence: __FILL IN — specify sheet name + row + column__

burn_rate.value: __FILL IN — FY2024 Actual total opex / 12 (in USD, after FX conversion if costs are in GBP)__

gross_margin_pct.value: __FILL IN — FY2024 Actual gross margin % (Revenue - COGS) / Revenue__

quarterly_actuals._note: Record individual quarterly actual values here for reference — these should NOT appear as current_state values

validation._note: The critical test here is that FY2024 Actual wins over Q4 2024 actual AND over FY2025E. All three may be present — verify the compiler's period_type labeling and truth-selection ordering is correct.

extraction_checks.note: Must be the full-year actual, not Q4-only or the FY2025E estimate

extraction_checks.expected_value: __FILL IN — monthly opex from FY2024 Actual ($000s sheet converted to USD)__
extraction_checks.note: Derived from costs sheet ($000s) with scale correction × 1000 and FX conversion if applicable

noise_checks.label: Single-quarter revenue stored as current-state annual
noise_checks.sql_filter: metric_key = 'revenue' AND period_label ILIKE 'Q% 2024' AND value > __FILL_IN_ANNUAL_THRESHOLD__
noise_checks.description: A quarterly revenue fact should never be stored with a value close to the full-year total. FILL_IN_ANNUAL_THRESHOLD should be ~75% of expected annual revenue.

noise_checks.label: $000s scale confusion: sub-1000 revenue row for a company with >$1M revenue
noise_checks.description: If the cost sheet denomination is $000s and a revenue figure leaks from that sheet unscaled, it will appear orders-of-magnitude too small. Threshold: update if company revenue is legitimately sub-$1K.

noise_checks.label: FY2025E revenue promoted as current-state (forecast over actual)
noise_checks.sql_filter: metric_key = 'revenue' AND period_label ILIKE '%2025E%' AND confidence = 'high'
noise_checks.description: Forecast estimate rows must not receive confidence=high — actual rows should dominate truth-selection

report_checks.label: current_state.revenue must be FY2024 Actual (not quarterly, not forecast)
report_checks.note: If system returns the FY2025E estimate or a single quarter, that is a temporal confusion failure

report_checks.label: current_state.burn_rate must be USD-denominated (post-FX)
report_checks.note: Wider tolerance here to allow for FX conversion variance; the key test is magnitude — GBP-only burn would be ~1.25x lower
